title: jmap: expose IPFS CID and operator signature as custom Email properties
description:
Why: The NNTP reader exposes X-Usenet-IPFS-CID and X-Usenet-IPFS-Sig as article headers and via XCID/XVERIFY commands. JMAP clients (including any usenet-ipfs-aware client) should be able to retrieve the same information without falling back to NNTP.

What:
1. Add x-usenet-ipfs-cid as a custom Email property in Email/get responses. This is the IPFS CID string for the article root block. JMAP RFC 8621 §5.1 allows vendor-prefixed custom properties.
2. Add x-usenet-ipfs-sig as a custom Email property: the base64url-encoded operator Ed25519 signature bytes from the X-Usenet-IPFS-Sig header.
3. Add a Usenet/verify method (or Email/verify) that accepts an emailId and optional expected CID, and returns: { cidMatch: bool, sigValid: bool }. This is the JMAP equivalent of XVERIFY SIG.
4. Advertise a custom capability urn:usenet-ipfs:jmap:cid in the session capabilities object so clients can detect support.

Standard JMAP clients that do not request x-usenet-ipfs-* properties receive no extra data and are unaffected.
